p: Give yourselves plenty of time, because this isn't a museum you dash round. Most visitors spend a good few hours here, and tank fans can happily stay all day. There's lots of walking between the halls, so comfy shoes help.

If you can, time your visit to coincide with one of the museum's big event days. TankFest, the annual summer event, sees historic vehicles out in the arena, and special days dedicated to Tiger 131 give you the chance to see a legend on the move. They're popular, so book well ahead.

There's more to do right on the doorstep. Monkey World, the ape rescue centre near Wool, is only a few minutes away and makes a brilliant second stop for families. Clouds Hill, the tiny cottage of T. E. Lawrence (Lawrence of Arabia), is also close by and now cared for by the National Trust.

The historic market town of Wareham, with its ancient earth walls and riverside quay, is just a short drive east. Head south instead and you're into the Isle of Purbeck, with Corfe Castle's dramatic ruins, the sandy beaches at Studland and plenty of coastal walking, so a visit here slots neatly into a longer Dorset break.
